I checked that this path persisted through the fix's parent and that the fix added a test for preserving verified findings when a reply exceeds the limits. A separate commit introduced both header controls with the native research pane, and the fix adopts a side-panel-only design.

fix_subject: fix: Gateway repeatedly rebuilds directory watches above 256 agents (#171805)
cause_quote: The initial watch cache used `if (preparedPaths.size <= 256)` as its eviction stop condition, then called `oldest.close()` on evicted entries, so a fleet with more than 256 distinct directories could never retain all its watches between walks.

summary: The fix sizes the prepared-path cache to the registered fleet, avoids full observer scans on routine watch changes, and limits per-agent startup directory preparation to the selected owner.
reasoning: The parent resolved directory identities directly, and PR #170467 introduced watch-backed reuse with the 256-entry FIFO cap in the same diff, so reuse across larger fleets was broken from its first release. I also checked that PR #171318 later added full observer scans when rescheduling recovery, which amplified the cost of the existing watch churn. The fix's test covers repeat walks at 64, 256, and 810 agents and checks for zero watch creation, watch closure, and realpath calls on the repeat walk.

reasoning: The pre-July checker already used an unscoped `git fetch --quiet --prune` when callers explicitly requested a refresh, and the available offline history did not establish where that behavior originated. PR #120506 changed the Gateway's status probe from `fetchGit: false` to `resolveStartupInstallStatus(configuredChannel === "dev")`, bringing that existing fetch into automatic Dev checks. PR #124611 later added a scoped detached fetch when a local upstream resolved, but a fresh checkout without that ref still fell through to the old broad fetch.

fix_subject: fix: preserve visitor revocation through provider failures (#153878)
cause_quote: The original revoke called `await this.policy.update((emails) => {` before changing the grant record, while the sweep selected only entries where `value.expiresAt !== null && value.expiresAt <= Date.now()`.

fix_subject: fix(agents): keep tool-authored replies from hiding unfinished work (#165291)

summary: The fix evaluates tool-authored replies against the finalized batch, keeps sibling failures eligible for model follow-up, and suppresses only the originating turn’s preamble.

It also added an embedded-runtime hook that used `context.toolResults.some(...)` to complete the turn on one eligible reply, regardless of the other results.
